short_description: System Issue: Employment Outcome Tracking Not Aligning with TtW Policy for Pre-existing Employment and PCW Participants
description:
Hi Digital Solutions Support Team

I would like to raise a system issue that has been identified through a recent policy review of a Transition to Work (TtW) participant record. Our investigation has identified that the Workforce Australia Online for Providers (WFAOP) system is currently allowing Employment Outcomes to track and become claimable in circumstances that are not consistent with TtW policy requirements.

Issue Summary

The issue relates to participants who:
Have an assessed Partial Capacity to Work (PCW).
Are in Pre-existing Employment and receiving an Income Support Payment at the commencement of the Outcome period.

Under current TtW policy, where an Employment Outcome is based on a Significant Increase in Pre-existing Employment, participants who are receiving an Income Support Payment must increase their earnings sufficiently to reduce their Income Support Payment to nil before an Employment Outcome can be achieved.

However, we have identified scenarios where the system is instead tracking Outcomes based on declared hours (JEHR average hours) rather than assessing the required income reduction to nil criteria. This appears to occur where the participant has a Part-Time Activity Test and/or a Partial Capacity to Work assessment. We assume the system is basing its assessment on a measurement against achieving the PCW hours such as 15 - 22 hours.

JSID 29033170, 12 Week Employment Outcome became available (effective date 28/07/2026) despite the participant not meeting the policy requirements for a Significant Increase in Pre-existing Employment. Instead, the system tracked the Outcome using an average hours methodology based on the participant's PCW and activity test settings.

Business Impact
This issue is creating situations where:

Employment Outcomes may be incorrectly generated and claimed and Providers receive Outcome Payments to which they are not entitled.
Recovery activity may subsequently be required.

Requested Investigation

Could the IT team please investigate:

Whether Outcome tracking logic for a Partial Capacity to Work participants receiving Income Support Payments is correctly applying the Significant Increase in Pre-existing Employment requirements within WFAOP.

Please let me know if further information or examples are required.

Kind regards,


Sheree O'Dea
Program  Manager

Transition to Work | Employment Services Programs Branch
Delivery and Partnerships Division
Australian Government Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
Phone (08) 8306 8669 | sheree.odea@dewr.gov.au

short_description: Azure SQL pool members are unable to Scope the ADMS production database.
description:
Hi,


The ADMS system has a dependency on these SQL build agent pools -

Settings * Agent pools (ADMS) - Settings<https://dev.azure.com/DigitalSolutionsDivision/ADMS/_settings/agentqueues?queueId=190&view=jobs>



[cid:image001.png@01DD570B.FC219920]


Over the last month during formal releases we've encountered many of these pool members failing to deploy database artefacts to the live ADMS Production DB.


This is an example of what we encounter during last nights ADMS release -

Pipelines - Run 20261006.1 logs<https://dev.azure.com/DigitalSolutionsDivision/ADMS/_build/results?buildId=1104160&view=logs&j=0ff409b1-0d17-50a2-fc4e-01f72eec43ff&t=423b483e-4f05-5139-03b6-c62b8492cc03&s=c2f23cc9-b49b-5971-bdfa-5e6430153f6c>


Error -
##[error]Error executing ADMSApprenticeship.dacpac, please ask a DBA *** Could not deploy package.Unable to connect to target server ''DBP_SKS_APPS01.application.enet,14331''. Please verify the connection information such as the server name, login credentials, and firewall rules for the target server.A network-related or instance-specific error occurred while establishing a connection to SQL Server. The server was not found or was not accessible. Verify that the instance name is correct and that SQL Server is configured to allow remote connections. (provider: TCP Provider, error: 0 - The wait operation timed out.)The wait operation timed out


This implies the SQL agent within the pool cannot scope our ADMS production database.  The workaround has been to keep retrying the failing pipeline, until we get allocated a healthy SQL agent.


These agent instances are known as being problematic - ECOEADO001_SQL_DO001_PRD01 and ECOEADO002_SQL_DO002_PRD01.  (There may be many more).


We need every SQL agent within this pool to be reviewed as to whether it can scope the ADMS DB and appropriate action taken.


Happy to assist.


Regards,

Jason

short_description: Remove Legacy Report Message Outlook Add-in
description:
Good afternoon Workplace Systems team,

The Cyber Governance and Education Team is seeking assistance to remove the legacy Report Message Outlook add-in.

A recent Microsoft update introduced built-in email reporting functionality within Outlook. As a result, users now have two separate options available to report suspicious emails. As the Microsoft-provided functionality now serves the same purpose, the legacy Report Message add-in is no longer required.

Removing the legacy add-in will reduce user confusion and provide staff with a single, consistent method for reporting suspicious emails.

There is a degree of urgency to this request as phishing awareness activities are currently underway as part of Cyber Awareness Month. Having two reporting buttons available during these activities may create unnecessary confusion for users when determining how to report suspicious emails.

We appreciate that this request comes at short notice. If possible, we would be grateful if this work could be prioritised.

This request has the approval of Cecilia Lau, Acting IT Security Advisor (ITSA).

If there are any other dependencies, approvals needed to progress this request, please let us know.

Microsoft recommends transitioning from the Report Message and Report Phishing add-ins to the built-in Outlook Report button and provides guidance on removing the legacy add-ins. Further information is available here:

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/submissions-users-report-message-add-in-configure

Your help is much appreciated.

Kind Regards,
Dan
